targetPath: /multi-country/interests/adventure/
kind: multi_country_interest_index
status: approved
buttonLabel: "Explore adventure routes across several countries"
lead: >-
  Adventure journeys across Latin America are best chosen by their activities and route, rather than by spectacular mountain photographs alone. Our itineraries let you combine a 4×4 expedition across Bolivia's highlands with the Atacama, explore Patagonia on a journey through Bolivia and Chile, or follow an extended route through Peru and Bolivia. Compare actual days outdoors, altitude, transport and time to recover.
---

## Adventures across several countries: the format matters more than border crossings

In our [multi-country adventure collection](/multi-country/interests/adventure/), you will find {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}. Yet the same theme covers journeys with very different physical demands: off-road expeditions across salt flats, glacier walks, visits to volcanic areas and guided tours of ancient cities. Mountains on an itinerary do not necessarily mean summit climbs, technical trekking or nights in tents.

Start with **what you most want to experience**: high-altitude landscapes, active hiking, or an extensive journey through several climate zones. Then check how many days are actually devoted to those activities, what transport is involved and which activities are included in the price.

For a particular activity within one country, also browse our main [Adventure Tours](/interests/adventure/) section. The benefit of these multi-country itineraries is the opportunity to travel between distinct natural regions on one trip.

## Atacama, Bolivia's lagoons and Peru: an Andean expedition by road

The [12-day Chile–Bolivia–Peru tour](/multi-country/tour/chile-bolivia-peru-group-12-days/) begins in Santiago and San Pedro de Atacama. A two-day 4×4 section follows through Bolivia's high-altitude lagoons, the Laguna Colorada area, the Sol de Mañana geysers and the [Uyuni Salt Flat](/bolivia/place/uyuni/). After La Paz, the journey continues to Lake Titicaca, Cusco and Machu Picchu.

This is **an adventure built around an off-road expedition and walks**. The main challenges are altitude, lengthy transfers, cold temperatures and limited infrastructure in some areas, not a compulsory mountaineering ascent. The programme specifically warns about elevations above 4,000 metres and possible symptoms of altitude sickness. Warm layered clothing, shoes for uneven ground, sun protection and adequate acclimatisation time are important.

The [12-day Peru and Bolivia with Uyuni itinerary](/multi-country/tour/peru-bolivia-uyuni-12-days/) has a different emphasis: [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/), Cusco, Titicaca, the Island of the Sun and the salt flat. It should not automatically be treated as a demanding hiking expedition; it combines sightseeing, overland transport and access to high-altitude sites. Compare overnight elevations and the number of hotel changes as well as overall duration.

## Bolivia and Chile: from the salt desert to Patagonian glaciers

The [16-day private Hidden Treasures of Bolivia and Chile tour](/multi-country/tour/bolivia-chile-hidden-treasures-16-days/) links La Paz and Uyuni with San Pedro de Atacama, the El Tatio geysers and Moon Valley. In the second half, travellers encounter Torres del Paine, the San Rafael Glacier, the Marble Caves and southern Chilean lakes. The journey ends in Santiago and Valparaíso.

Conditions change particularly sharply along this route. Bolivia brings high elevations and exposed salt plains; the Atacama brings dry air, strong sunlight and cool nights; Patagonia brings wind, glacial water and potential changes to boat-trip schedules. Pack a separate set of clothes for the southern section and check which activities on the water depend on the weather.

The programme includes land and boat excursions, but it does not specify a difficult independent ascent of the summits in Torres del Paine. A multi-day hiking programme would be a separate route requirement to discuss when choosing a journey.

## The wider South America journey: what adventure means on a long route

The [32-day tour through eight countries](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) includes Bolivia's lagoons and Uyuni, an Andean crossing to Peru, a visit to the Galápagos, and natural areas in Brazil and Argentina. However, many days are devoted to city tours, flights and road transfers. Adventure stops are part of an overview journey, rather than a specialist expedition.

For these programmes, compare the proportion of days spent genuinely outdoors and the number of travel days between them. Sometimes a shorter journey with a substantial expedition component provides more direct experience than an itinerary covering many countries in brief visits.

| Format | Main focus |
|---|---|
| Chile – Bolivia – Peru | Altitude, 4×4 vehicles, the Andes |
| Bolivia – Chile | Desert and glaciers |
| Peru – Bolivia | Heritage sites and Uyuni |
| Extended itinerary | A variety of regions |

## Altitude, seasons and physical preparation

Altitude is the main physiological consideration on many Andean adventure routes. A rapid ascent from lowlands to La Paz or Bolivia's highlands calls for caution. According to CDC guidance, the risk of altitude sickness primarily depends on elevation and the speed of ascent; physical fitness does not guarantee protection. When planning, consider the altitude of **overnight stays** and allow time to acclimatise.

In Uyuni and around the lagoons, rain can change driving conditions and the appearance of the salt flat: a reflective surface looks very different from a dry white plain. In Patagonia, strong winds and weather restrictions affect some water excursions. Instead of seeking one universally "best month for all South America", choose a season for your main activity and then check the other sections.

Before booking, confirm the character of walking sections, footwear requirements, options for reducing exertion and whether the itinerary suits your health. Walks mentioned in a national park description are not necessarily organised trekking excursions with guides and equipment.

## Coordinating countries without losing your active days

Travelling between Chile, Bolivia and Peru takes time for border procedures, connections and changes in elevation. A flight often reaches the expedition's starting point, followed by a jeep itinerary with little choice of intermediate stops. In Patagonia, weather windows for boat trips can determine the journey's timing.

We help coordinate the country sequence, road transfers, local guides, accommodation and time buffers. Entry and transit rules are checked for each traveller's nationality, along with insurance coverage for the selected activities. Equipment inclusions, baggage arrangements and the option to move an excursion to a different day must be taken from the actual offer, rather than assumed to be part of the base price.

## Frequently asked questions about multi-country adventure tours

### Do I need to be an experienced mountaineer to visit Uyuni?

No. On the itineraries described here, Uyuni is visited mainly by vehicle, with stops and walks. Altitude still matters, so physical demands and acclimatisation need separate consideration.

### Can I combine the Atacama and Patagonia in one journey?

Yes. The [16-day Bolivia–Chile programme](/multi-country/tour/bolivia-chile-hidden-treasures-16-days/) includes both. You will need different clothing for each region, and flights are required to travel between the north and south.

### Do these tours include genuine multi-day trekking?

The programmes discussed here mainly combine sightseeing walks with vehicle travel. If your goal is a dedicated multi-day trek, select a suitable day-by-day itinerary and confirm difficulty, guides and equipment.

### Which matters more when choosing: the season or the duration?

Start with the season and conditions for the main activity. Even a long tour can be poorly suited if weather restrictions affect its key glacier or high-altitude section. Then choose the required length and leave room for transfers.

targetPath: /multi-country/interests/beach-holidays/
kind: multi_country_interest_index
status: approved
buttonLabel: "Explore beach itineraries across several countries"
lead: >-
  On a multi-country journey, beach days are best planned as a meaningful part of the itinerary rather than as a brief stop between airports. Our programmes combine the sea with Maya archaeology, South American cities, tropical parks and waterfalls. Your choice depends on where the beach stay is scheduled: on the Caribbean Sea, the Pacific or the Atlantic coast.
---

## Beach holidays on multi-country journeys: where to leave time for the sea

**A good multi-country itinerary with beach time leaves enough time to enjoy the beach itself.** Arriving in the evening, sleeping in a coastal hotel and leaving the next morning is a different experience from spending two or three free days by the sea. Start by identifying specific relaxation days in the itinerary, then consider how many countries can be included without constant transfers.

Our catalogue features {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} combining beach holidays with visits to several main countries. **The beach portion may take place in just one country on the route.** On an Argentina–Brazil journey, for example, sightseeing covers Buenos Aires, Patagonia and Iguazu, while warm ocean beaches are scheduled in Brazil. On a trip through Guatemala, Honduras and Belize, ancient Maya cities come before days at sea on Belize's islands.

Three useful comparisons are [Argentina and Brazil with beach time](/multi-country/argentina_brazil/interests/beach-holidays/), [Guatemala and Belize with a beach stay](/multi-country/belize_guatemala/interests/beach-holidays/) and [Costa Rica and Nicaragua with beach time](/multi-country/costa-rica_nicaragua/interests/beach-holidays/). They differ in sea, season, duration of coastal stops and included excursions.

## The Caribbean: Belize after Maya heritage sites

The [Guatemala, Honduras and Belize tour](/multi-country/tour/guatemala-honduras-belize/) begins with Antigua, Lake Atitlán, Copán, Quiriguá and Tikal. After several days among colonial towns and archaeological sites, the journey moves to Ambergris Caye in Belize. The programme includes marine activities and dedicated days near the reef. This suits travellers looking to end an extensive cultural journey by the Caribbean Sea.

Another option is [Cancun and Belize in 11 days](/multi-country/tour/cancun-belize-11-days/). The Mexico section combines Cancun with Chichén Itzá, Tulum and Cobá before the journey continues to Ambergris Caye. The itinerary includes the Hol Chan Marine Reserve; check the tour description for the format and possible restrictions of individual activities. Belize's islands and Mexico's beaches complement different cultural experiences here.

For a Caribbean holiday, distinguish **beach relaxation**, **snorkelling** and **scuba diving** in advance. A reef mentioned in an itinerary does not mean that certified diving is included in the price. Decide whether boat rides, snorkelling or additional outings matter most before selecting a particular tour.

## Brazil's Atlantic coast after mountains, cities and waterfalls

In South America, the beach is often the finale to a long sightseeing journey. The [Argentina and Brazil tour ending at Praia da Pipa](/multi-country/tour/argentina-brazil-buenos-aires-el-calafate-iguazu-pipa-11-days/) starts in Buenos Aires, visits Perito Moreno Glacier and both sides of Iguazu Falls, then ends with free time on Brazil's coast. After Patagonia's winds and a busy excursion schedule, several days without early departures beside the ocean are especially welcome.

The [13-day Brazil itinerary including Iguazu, Lençóis Maranhenses and Pipa](/multi-country/tour/brazil-rio-iguazu-lencois-natal-pipa-13-days/) also visits the Argentine side of Iguazu. Its main beach section is again in Brazil: the journey passes the sandy dunes and lagoons of Lençóis Maranhenses and ends near Pipa. This offers a substantially different experience from a few days on an urban beach in Rio.

A further contrast is the [Peru and Brazil tour ending in Búzios](/multi-country/tour/peru-machu-picchu-brazil-rio-beaches/). In Peru, the route includes high-altitude monuments and Machu Picchu, followed by the Brazilian section with Iguazu and Rio; the days in Búzios are for the sea. Beach time works particularly well after the Andes, not as a replacement for exploring Peru.

## Central America's Pacific coast

The [Costa Rica–Nicaragua itinerary](/multi-country/tour/costa-rica-nicaragua/) combines Costa Rica's national parks, volcanoes and a coffee plantation with colonial Granada and Lake Nicaragua. Days on the Pacific coast are scheduled after the return to Costa Rica. This arrangement suits travellers who want an active first section and a relaxed finish.

On the [Panama, Costa Rica and Nicaragua programme](/multi-country/tour/panama-costa-rica-nicaragua/), coastal scenery comes together with Manuel Antonio National Park, cloud forests, volcanoes and Nicaraguan cities. A visit to a seaside national park is different from a completely free beach day. The itinerary and number of nights near the water matter more than merely reaching the ocean.

Climate differs between Costa Rica's two coasts. On the Pacific side, the dry season generally runs from mid-December through late April, although local conditions depend on the region. This is guidance for choosing dates, not a promise of sunshine every day. On a journey crossing several climate zones, we help match travel dates to destinations and leave sensible time buffers for transfers.

## Comparing the routes without confusion

| Option | Main appeal |
|---|---|
| Guatemala, Belize | Maya heritage + Caribbean Sea |
| Mexico, Belize | Maya cities + reef |
| Argentina, Brazil | Patagonia or Iguazu + beach |
| Peru, Brazil | Andes + Atlantic |
| Costa Rica, Nicaragua | Nature + Pacific-coast finale |

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_source_gvatemala_gonduras_i_beliz,tour_source_kankun_beliz,tour_argentina_brazil_pipa_11d,tour_source_tur_v_peru_i_braziliyu,tour_source_costa_rica_nicaragua_ru}}

When comparing tours, look at full days by the sea, how often hotels and flights change, the location of the specific beach area, swimming conditions and activities actually included. On multi-country journeys, it is particularly helpful to leave a free day after the last long transfer. A nearby sea and a coastal hotel do not automatically provide uninterrupted beach relaxation.

We organise the sequence of cities, flights and road journeys around your priorities. If the sea is your main goal, build the itinerary around nights on the coast. If Machu Picchu, Maya cities or Iguazu matter more, put beach time after the main excursions. For more options focused on this interest, see our [Beach Holidays](/interests/beach-holidays/) collection; for broader geography, explore [multi-country tours](/multi-country/).

## Frequently asked questions about multi-country beach holidays

### Will there be beach time in every country?

No. The thematic label applies to the tour as a whole. On an Argentina–Brazil journey, the beach may be only in Brazil; on a Guatemala–Honduras–Belize journey, the sea section is concentrated in Belize. Check the actual days and overnight stays, not just the country list.

### Can Machu Picchu be combined with a beach holiday?

Yes. The [Peru and Brazil programme](/multi-country/tour/peru-machu-picchu-brazil-rio-beaches/) does so. After the Peru sightseeing section, the itinerary includes Iguazu, Rio and a stay in Búzios. Moving from highlands to the tropics requires suitable clothing and allowances for flights.

### Where is it best to combine ancient Maya cities with the sea?

Consider [Guatemala and Belize](/multi-country/belize_guatemala/interests/beach-holidays/) or the Cancun–Belize programme. They differ in the archaeological sites included and the time available by the coast.

### Which itinerary is better for several free days at the end?

Compare [Argentina and Brazil with Pipa](/multi-country/tour/argentina-brazil-buenos-aires-el-calafate-iguazu-pipa-11-days/) with [Costa Rica and Nicaragua](/multi-country/tour/costa-rica-nicaragua/). Both place beach days towards the end, but their countries, flights and climates differ considerably.

targetPath: /multi-country/interests/coffee-tours/
kind: multi_country_interest_index
status: approved
buttonLabel: "Explore coffee journeys through Costa Rica and Nicaragua"
lead: >-
  On a trip through Costa Rica and Nicaragua, the coffee experience takes place at Costa Rica's working Doka Estate plantation. The visit follows the bean from cultivation to roasting, while the rest of the journey explores volcanoes, tropical forests and colonial Granada. We offer a standard 13-day itinerary and a private 12-day VIP alternative.
---

## Multi-country coffee journeys: Costa Rica and Nicaragua

**A coffee tour becomes far more engaging when you see where coffee grows and how freshly picked fruit is processed into beans ready for roasting.** In Costa Rica, such a visit can be combined with a journey into neighbouring Nicaragua. The itinerary covers two countries, but its principal coffee experience is at one specific Costa Rican estate.

Our catalogue includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} across multiple countries with a substantial coffee component. Currently, this involves the [Costa Rica and Nicaragua combination](/multi-country/costa-rica_nicaragua/interests/coffee-tours/). It is important to distinguish the roles of the stops: **coffee production is explored in Costa Rica, whereas Nicaragua's section focuses on Granada, Masaya Volcano, Lake Nicaragua and other locations in the itinerary**. An additional tour of a Nicaraguan coffee farm should not be assumed to be included unless the programme specifically says so.

Compare the [13-day Costa Rica–Nicaragua journey](/multi-country/tour/costa-rica-nicaragua/) with the [12-day VIP tour featuring a private flight](/multi-country/tour/costa-rica-nicaragua-vip-private-plane/). Both visit Doka Estate, but their other excursions, transport, durations and placement of free days differ.

## Doka Estate: how coffee is grown and processed

Doka Estate is part of the introduction to Costa Rica. During the visit, travellers learn about coffee cultivation, harvesting, bean processing and roasting. You can see the stages of production on one working estate rather than simply buying a souvenir packet at the airport.

On the [13-day Costa Rica–Nicaragua programme](/multi-country/tour/costa-rica-nicaragua/), the coffee tour takes place on day two. After the plantation, the route continues to Poás Volcano and La Paz Waterfalls. One day brings together farming traditions, volcanic landscapes and humid tropical forest. The excursion description includes cultivation, harvesting, processing, roasting and the opportunity to buy coffee at the estate.

On the [VIP itinerary](/multi-country/tour/costa-rica-nicaragua-vip-private-plane/), Doka Estate is visited on day six. This programme explicitly includes preparing and tasting coffee after learning about production. Poás Volcano and La Paz Waterfalls also form part of the coffee day. This is a meaningful distinction: **a tasting at the plantation** is directly confirmed on the VIP itinerary.

## Standard 13-day tour: a coffee stop and national parks

The [13-day Costa Rica and Nicaragua itinerary](/multi-country/tour/costa-rica-nicaragua/) begins in San José. After Doka and Poás Volcano, it continues through Tortuguero, the Arenal region and Monteverde. In Costa Rica, travellers experience canals and tropical forest, volcanic landscapes and cloud forests.

The Nicaragua section then follows: Granada, Masaya Volcano, Lake Nicaragua and its islands. At the end, the journey returns to Costa Rica, with time scheduled on the Pacific coast. The tour combines coffee with diverse natural and cultural sites and leaves time by the ocean.

**Coffee occupies one substantial day within a wider journey.** Choose this route if you want to learn about local coffee production while also visiting wildlife habitats, volcanoes, historic cities and the coast.

## 12-day VIP tour: coffee, chocolate and a private flight

The [Costa Rica and Nicaragua VIP tour](/multi-country/tour/costa-rica-nicaragua-vip-private-plane/) is a private 12-day itinerary. Its Costa Rica section includes both Doka Estate and a separate cacao and chocolate experience. Other stops include Arenal Volcano, Río Celeste, hanging bridges and nature excursions.

After the busy opening section, a private flight takes travellers from Costa Rica to Nicaragua. The journey includes Granada, Lake Nicaragua and Masaya Volcano, with its final days beside Apoyo Lagoon. It offers a different balance: active and culinary excursions followed by a quieter break.

**Coffee and chocolate experiences are separate activities.** Chocolate is made from cacao, whose cultivation and processing differ from coffee. On the VIP tour, the two complement each other and introduce two regional products. However, the private flight, accommodation, excursions and additional services must be checked against the specific offer. The VIP designation alone does not establish that every option is included.

## Comparing the two itineraries

| Feature | Costa Rica–Nicaragua, 13 days | VIP tour, 12 days |
|---|---|---|
| Coffee plantation | Doka Estate, day two | Doka Estate, day six |
| Coffee experience | Growing, harvesting, processing and roasting | The same processes plus tasting |
| Other culinary activities | Main focus on coffee | Separate chocolate programme |
| Nature stops | Tortuguero, Arenal, Monteverde | Arenal, Río Celeste, other activities |
| Nicaragua finale | Granada and a return to the Pacific coast | Granada and relaxation at Apoyo Lagoon |

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_source_costa_rica_nicaragua_ru,tour_source_vip_kosta_rika_nikaragua}}

The choice depends on the role coffee should play in your holiday. For a plantation visit combined with national parks and beach time, consider the 13-day route. For tasting, chocolate making and private transfers, compare the VIP alternative.

## What to know before visiting a coffee farm

A visit is more rewarding when you ask about production: how ripe cherries are picked, what happens after the pulp is removed, how beans are dried and sorted, and why roasting changes the flavour. At the estate, you may be able to compare processed beans with a finished drink if a tasting is included in the programme.

Poás Volcano lies at altitude, so the weather may be cooler than in warm San José and cloud sometimes obscures the crater. Bring comfortable shoes and light rain protection for a day combining the farm, volcano and waterfalls. The order of visits depends on actual conditions and access to each site.

Travel between Costa Rica and Nicaragua involves either a border crossing or a private flight, depending on the itinerary. Entry rules and documents depend on nationality and route and must be checked for the actual travel dates. Where a journey involves several transfers, it is useful to know in advance where hotels change and how much free time remains after excursions.

We can help compare both itineraries, clarify the coffee programme and agree on the other stops. You can also browse [all coffee tours](/interests/coffee-tours/) or the [Costa Rica and Nicaragua catalogue](/multi-country/costa-rica_nicaragua/).

## Frequently asked questions about multi-country coffee tours

### Where exactly does the coffee tour take place?

On the existing Ada Tours multi-country itineraries, Doka Estate is in **Costa Rica**. Nicaragua's section is devoted to other stops; a Nicaraguan coffee tour should not be assumed solely from the theme.

### Can I see the full coffee-production process?

Yes. Both programmes introduce cultivation, harvesting, processing and roasting at Doka. The VIP itinerary additionally specifies preparing and tasting the drink.

### How do the 12- and 13-day itineraries differ?

The [13-day journey](/multi-country/tour/costa-rica-nicaragua/) spends considerable time at Tortuguero, Monteverde, Nicaragua and the Pacific coast. The [12-day VIP tour](/multi-country/tour/costa-rica-nicaragua-vip-private-plane/) adds a chocolate experience, private flight and relaxation at Apoyo Lagoon.

### Is the journey suitable for people who do not drink coffee?

Yes, if you are interested in volcanoes, tropical forests, colonial architecture and national parks. The coffee visit provides an introduction to local production, while most of the itinerary covers other experiences.

### Do I have to book the plantation excursion separately?

Doka Estate is already listed in both programmes. To determine which services are included in the final cost of a particular tour, consult its pricing and inclusions sections. Do not assume extra tastings or visits to other estates are included.

targetPath: /multi-country/interests/cruises-and-expeditions/
kind: multi_country_interest_index
status: approved
buttonLabel: "Explore cruises and expeditions across several countries"
lead: >-
  A cruise through the fjords of Chile and Argentina, a maritime expedition to Antarctica and a river journey on the Peruvian Amazon differ in route, landing conditions and preparation. We combine time on the water with overland journeys through several countries, from Patagonia and Tierra del Fuego to Peru, Bolivia and Ecuador.
---

## Multi-country cruises and expeditions: from Patagonia to the Amazon

**For a multi-country cruise, first establish which parts you will spend on board and which will be spent travelling overland.** Some programmes are almost entirely aboard expedition ships, while others feature a few days on a river cruise within a long land journey. The distinction affects cabin selection, flights, baggage and the chance of itinerary changes due to weather.

Our catalogue features {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} with cruise or expedition elements and several main countries. Options include [Argentina and Chile](/multi-country/argentina_chile/interests/cruises-and-expeditions/) with fjord voyages, [Argentina, Chile and Antarctica](/multi-country/antarctica_argentina_chile/interests/cruises-and-expeditions/) with a Drake Passage crossing, [Peru and Bolivia](/multi-country/bolivia_peru/interests/cruises-and-expeditions/) with an Amazon cruise and [Peru and Ecuador](/multi-country/ecuador_peru/interests/cruises-and-expeditions/), where river cruising is combined with the Andes and Galápagos Islands.

Here the term "expedition" describes the format of a particular journey. A short boat ride during a sightseeing day is not a multi-day cruise, while a visit to the Galápagos Islands does not automatically mean the entire Ecuador section is spent on a cruise ship.

## Chilean fjords: nine days from Puerto Montt to Ushuaia

[Patagonia and Chilean Fjords](/multi-country/tour/patagonia-chilean-fjords/) is a nine-day sea journey. The ship departs from Puerto Montt in Chile and travels through Patagonia's islands, fjords and channels, entering the areas of San Rafael and Bernardo O'Higgins national parks. It then continues via the Strait of Magellan and Tierra del Fuego to Ushuaia in Argentina.

Much of the experience comes from being at sea: mountains and glaciers emerge around bends in narrow waterways, the expedition team gives lectures and there may be landings and outings in small boats. The programme mentions Zodiac boats near the glaciers. Such excursions depend on sea conditions, wind and whether the shore can be approached safely.

This itinerary suits travellers who want to see southern Patagonia from the water. Chile and Argentina are the two main countries, but the time on land is not comparable to a full land tour of both. Before buying flights, confirm the embarkation and disembarkation ports, overnight arrangements and return journey from the other country.

## Tierra del Fuego: a shorter journey between Chile and Argentina

[Fjords of Tierra del Fuego](/multi-country/tour/tierra-del-fuego-fjords/) offers a different option: **five days aboard a ship from Punta Arenas to Ushuaia**. Starting on the Chilean side, the voyage crosses the Strait of Magellan and Tierra del Fuego channels, visiting Ainsworth Bay, the Tucker Islets, the Pia Glacier area, Wulaia Bay and Cape Horn. It ends in Argentina's Ushuaia.

Compare it with the nine-day route from Puerto Montt if your time is limited. Both cross Chile and Argentina, but use different ports and cover different parts of Patagonia. The shorter cruise may leave more time for an independently arranged visit to Buenos Aires, Santiago or national parks before or after sailing, provided those days are added to the journey separately.

Landings at Cape Horn and other small shore outings depend on weather. The captain and expedition team make decisions for safety, so no landing can be guaranteed unconditionally.

## Antarctica: leaving Ushuaia by sea and returning to Chile by air

The six-day [Antarctica Express](/multi-country/tour/antarctica-patagonia-express-air-cruise-6-days/) combines Argentina, Chile and Antarctica in one expedition plan. Passengers board in Ushuaia. The route goes through the Beagle Channel and Chilean waters towards Cape Horn, then crosses the Drake Passage to the South Shetland Islands. The Antarctic section ends on King George Island, with a return flight to Punta Arenas.

The key logistical difference is that **the start and finish are in different countries**. Plan air tickets to arrive in Argentina and depart from Chile, including regional flights. Flying out of Antarctica depends on suitable weather, as do Zodiac excursions on the water.

Antarctica is a continent under an international governance regime, not a third country on the route. Preparation therefore involves entry requirements for Argentina and Chile and separate rules for visiting environmentally sensitive Antarctic areas. Expedition operators have biosecurity procedures, including cleaning clothing and equipment before landings.

## Amazon and Andes: a river cruise within a longer journey

On the [18-day Peru and Bolivia VIP itinerary](/multi-country/tour/peru-bolivia-amazon-cruise-vip-18-days/), the river cruise takes place **in Peru**. After Lima, travellers continue to Iquitos for a four-day, three-night AQUA EXPEDITION programme aboard Aria Amazon. The journey then proceeds by land and air to Cusco, Machu Picchu, Lake Titicaca and Bolivia's Uyuni Salt Flat.

The combination of two very different regions is the appeal: humid Amazon rainforest and the high-altitude landscapes of the Andes. The Aria Amazon cruise offers a view of the river and protected areas from the water, with smaller-boat excursions on certain days. The Bolivia section is overland; the river cruise does not extend automatically into the second country.

The [18-day Peru and Ecuador with Galápagos itinerary](/multi-country/tour/peru-ecuador-galapagos-luxury-18-days/) also features Aria Amazon in the Peruvian Amazon, followed by Cusco and Machu Picchu. Ecuador's section includes Quito, cloud forest and the Galápagos Islands. Read its accommodation and inter-island transport arrangements separately: **Galápagos excursions alone do not establish that there is a multi-day cruise around the archipelago**.

## Comparing cruise itineraries

| Programme | Cruise section | Onward journey |
|---|---|---|
| Patagonia and Chilean Fjords, 9 days | Sea voyage through southern Chile | Disembarkation in Ushuaia, Argentina |
| Fjords of Tierra del Fuego, 5 days | Punta Arenas to Ushuaia | Finishes in Argentina |
| Antarctica Express, 6 days | Ushuaia to Antarctica | Flight to Punta Arenas |
| Peru and Bolivia, 18 days | Aria Amazon in Peru | Andes, Titicaca, Uyuni |
| Peru and Ecuador, 18 days | Aria Amazon in Peru | Machu Picchu and Galápagos |

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_source_patagoniya_i_chilijskie_fordy,tour_source_fordy_ognennoj_zemli,tour_source_antarktida_ekspress_vozdushnyj_kruiz,tour_source_vip_tur_v_boliviyu_i_peru_na_18_dnej_s_kruizom_po_amazonke,tour_source_lyuksovyj_tur_v_peru_i_ehkvador_s_galapagosami_na_18_dnej}}

Begin by comparing **time aboard the vessel** and the land portion of each itinerary. Then check departure and arrival ports, the number of international and domestic flights, and landing conditions. Meals, cabin categories, excursions, port fees and transfers should be checked within each specific programme, as cruise inclusions vary.

In expedition regions, leave extra time after the cruise. This is particularly important for a Drake Passage crossing or a flight from an Antarctic island, where the weather may affect the schedule. On the Amazon, consider seasonal water-level changes and their effect on river routes rather than planning solely around the general holiday calendar.

We help coordinate cruise and land sections and agree on their starting and finishing points. More options are available in [Cruises and Expeditions](/interests/cruises-and-expeditions/), with the full geographic selection in our [multi-country travel catalogue](/multi-country/).

## Frequently asked questions about multi-country cruises

### Can I start a cruise in Chile and finish in Argentina?

Yes. [Fjords of Tierra del Fuego](/multi-country/tour/tierra-del-fuego-fjords/) travels from Punta Arenas to Ushuaia, while the [nine-day Chilean fjords route](/multi-country/tour/patagonia-chilean-fjords/) goes from Puerto Montt to Ushuaia. Flights need to be arranged for the different cities.

### Does an Antarctic air-cruise avoid all sea crossings?

No. On [Antarctica Express](/multi-country/tour/antarctica-patagonia-express-air-cruise-6-days/), the Drake Passage is crossed by sea on the outbound journey to Antarctica; the return leg from King George Island to Chile is by air, weather permitting.

### Are Amazon cruises included on the Peru and Bolivia itinerary?

Yes. The [18-day programme](/multi-country/tour/peru-bolivia-amazon-cruise-vip-18-days/) includes an Aria Amazon river cruise near Iquitos in Peru. Afterwards, the journey continues to Machu Picchu, Titicaca and Uyuni.

### Are landings at Cape Horn and in Antarctica guaranteed?

No. Landings depend on weather, sea conditions, safety and decisions made by the expedition crew. Check the alternative arrangements for itinerary changes.

### Do cruises and expeditions require the same preparation?

No. Antarctic journeys put particular emphasis on biosecurity and weather risk. Amazon river cruises involve a humid tropical climate and local water-transport conditions. Both require a careful reading of the specific programme before booking.

## Culture and history across several countries: choosing an itinerary

A journey through several countries is rewarding when each stage introduces another historical era, urban tradition or cultural experience. Our catalogue includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} with culture and history themes and several main countries. Some concentrate on archaeology; others combine historic city centres, museums, local traditions and natural landmarks.

The most useful starting point is **which places you actually visit and what the programme includes**. A day in one country might feature a museum or archaeological site, or it might consist almost entirely of a transfer and an overnight stay. The overall theme does not turn every day into a history excursion.

For an initial comparison, look at these thematic multi-country programmes alongside our [general Culture and History section](/interests/culture-and-history/). This page concerns itineraries that cross borders; the general section also includes single-country journeys.

## Four different ways to discover Latin America

### The Maya world: Guatemala, Belize and neighbouring countries

The [Guatemala and Belize cultural collection](/multi-country/belize_guatemala/interests/culture-and-history/) gives particular attention to archaeological monuments and living traditions. The existing [Guatemala and Belize: Into the Maya World tour](/multi-country/tour/guatemala-belize-maya-world-12-days/) includes Lake Atitlán and its villages, Tikal, San Ignacio and other stops. Compare the specific ancient cities scheduled for visits and the time remaining after transfers, rather than simply counting all ancient cities mentioned in a country's description.

The longer [eight-country Central America itinerary](/multi-country/tour/central-america-8-countries-26-days/) includes Teotihuacán and Chichén Itzá in Mexico, Caracol in Belize, Tikal in Guatemala and Copán in Honduras. Colonial towns, craft villages near Atitlán and cultural encounters in other countries are added. This sequence reveals distinctions between archaeological complexes, historic cities and present-day regional life. The broad coverage comes at the cost of many transfers and hotel changes.

If Maya cities are your main goal, the more compact Guatemala–Belize combination usually allows a more focused visit. The eight-country journey suits those who want to compare the different cultural and natural zones of Central America.

### The Andes: Peru and Bolivia

[Culture and history tours through Peru and Bolivia](/multi-country/bolivia_peru/interests/culture-and-history/) link Lima, Cusco and Machu Picchu to highland cities and Bolivia's cultural heritage. The [Peru and Bolivia programme](/multi-country/tour/peru-bolivia/) includes Lima, Cusco, the Sacred Valley of the Incas, Machu Picchu, Lake Titicaca and La Paz. This is a comparatively focused journey from Inca monuments to life in the modern Andean region.

The more extensive [six-country journey from Rio to Machu Picchu](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-6-countries-20-days/) adds a historical stop at Tiwanaku on the Bolivia–Peru section. It offers a comparison of different civilisational centres, but some days are devoted to long-distance journeys, flights and transfers between high-altitude regions.

Altitude affects the pace of a cultural journey through the Andes. Visiting an archaeological complex, travelling for several hours and walking around a high-altitude city may feel quite different immediately after arriving from the coast. Consider the sequence of overnight stays, walking tours and acclimatisation, particularly if lengthy sightseeing walks are planned.

### Atlantic cities: Brazil, Argentina and Uruguay

The [three-country Atlantic cultural itinerary](/multi-country/argentina_brazil_uruguay/interests/culture-and-history/) tells different stories. On the [13-day Brazil, Argentina and Uruguay tour](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-uruguay-13-days/), travellers begin with Rio de Janeiro and Iguazu, followed by Buenos Aires, Colonia del Sacramento, Montevideo and Punta del Este. One day introduces gaucho traditions on a ranch.

Historical interest here centres on city life, colonial architecture, the development of port cities and regional traditions. Crossing the Río de la Plata is a meaningful part of the route: it connects Buenos Aires with Uruguay, so port formalities and crossing time must be considered alongside the time allocated to excursions.

For an archaeology-focused journey, this itinerary offers fewer dedicated days than the Andean or Central American options. Instead, it provides a relatively coherent introduction to neighbouring countries through city walks and breaks.

### The Guianas: colonial heritage and Maroon culture

The [Guyana, Suriname and French Guiana culture collection](/multi-country/french-guiana_guyana_suriname/interests/culture-and-history/) tells a story unlike a classic Andean journey. The [Three Guianas tour](/multi-country/tour/suriname-guyana-french-guiana/) begins in Georgetown, then continues to Paramaribo, old plantations and the Suriname River. In French Guiana, it visits islands associated with the history of the penal system and Kourou. In Suriname, it introduces Maroon communities and places away from the capital.

Borders require special attention: French Guiana has a different political and legal status from Guyana and Suriname. Entry rules and documents depend on nationality and the order in which borders are crossed. The programme provides an opportunity to explore colonial history, the lives of descendants of African communities and the region's contemporary culture on the same journey.

|---|---|
| Maya cities and crafts | Guatemala and Belize |
| Incas, Titicaca and the Andes | Peru and Bolivia |
| Port cities and gauchos | Brazil, Argentina and Uruguay |
| Colonial history and Maroon communities | The Three Guianas |

Its historical excursions alternate with nature and travel days, making it different from a focused cultural itinerary through Peru and Bolivia alone.

## Coordinating countries so that history is not lost to transfers

### Allow time for each visit

One substantial day at a large archaeological complex provides more than three brief roadside stops. In Central America, distinguish the transfer to a monument from the excursion on site and time left in the surrounding town. In the Andes, altitude and distances between Cusco, Titicaca and La Paz create similar constraints.

When arranging a journey, we match the sites that interest you with its realistic duration: which visits are included, which are optional, and how many hours are needed for travel, guiding and hotel check-in. If time is limited, reducing the number of countries may be better than leaving historic monuments as names in a list of stops.

### Account for each border's formalities

Multi-country travel requires checking entry rules for each traveller's citizenship. Consider entry into the next country and re-entry if the route returns through a country already visited. Transit rules can also depend on the airline and connecting airport.

The ferry between Argentina and Uruguay creates one set of logistical requirements; travel through the Three Guianas creates another. There is no universal set of documents for "all of Latin America". We help establish what needs checking for the itinerary and nationality, while official entry conditions should be confirmed before travel.

### Confirm museum and excursion hours

Museums, archaeological sites, religious buildings and local cultural events have their own hours and visiting rules. A long drive may lead to arrival after closing, even when the site appears in the itinerary. For important stops, agree on the weekday and order of excursions in advance, with spare time where needed.

Cultural experiences also take different forms: archaeological visits, walking through a historic centre, meeting artisans or attending a performance. They are not interchangeable. Identify two or three main events you most want to experience, then confirm that the itinerary gives them sufficient time.

## What to choose for different trip lengths

For a shorter journey with a clear cultural focus, consider two neighbouring countries and a few major sites. [Peru and Bolivia](/multi-country/bolivia_peru/interests/culture-and-history/) are suitable for Andean history, while [Guatemala and Belize](/multi-country/belize_guatemala/interests/culture-and-history/) are excellent for exploring Maya monuments.

For a combination of architecture, traditions and nature across several regions, a longer itinerary may be preferable. Consider actual days in each place, not just the number of countries. The [six-country Latin America tour](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-6-countries-20-days/) and [eight-country Central America itinerary](/multi-country/tour/central-america-8-countries-26-days/) offer different histories, geographies and transfer patterns.

You can also compare [all multi-country tours](/multi-country/) with [culture-focused single-country journeys](/interests/culture-and-history/). Spending more time in one country often allows more visits to museums, cities and archaeological complexes, if these matter more than geographical breadth.

## Frequently asked questions about multi-country cultural tours

### Can I see Machu Picchu and Tiwanaku on one journey?

Yes. This combination features on some extended Peru and Bolivia routes, including the [six-country tour from Rio to Machu Picchu](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-6-countries-20-days/). Check the specific days: merely listing both countries does not guarantee visits to both monuments.

### How do I choose between Guatemala with Belize and Peru with Bolivia?

For Maya cities and Central American craft traditions, choose [Guatemala and Belize](/multi-country/belize_guatemala/interests/culture-and-history/). For Inca heritage, the Sacred Valley, Machu Picchu and highland Andean culture, choose [Peru and Bolivia](/multi-country/bolivia_peru/interests/culture-and-history/). For the latter, also consider altitude and the pace of travel.

### Does every country on a cultural tour receive the same number of excursions?

No. One country on a multi-country itinerary may include several museum and heritage days; another may involve just a border crossing or brief stop. Read the day-by-day itinerary and descriptions of included excursions rather than relying on the tour's theme alone.

### Should I choose the route with the maximum number of countries?

No. If you prioritise specific monuments, an extra country may simply add flights and road transfers. Wider geography is valuable when it includes genuinely different cultural sites you want to experience.

### How can I tell in advance which cultural visits are included?

Distinguish compulsory excursions, independent free time and optional activities. Read the chosen [multi-country tour](/multi-country/) and its inclusions. We can help clarify the order and duration of important visits when agreeing on the programme.
